question: Which of the following elements has three valence electrons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Al (Aluminum)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aluminum (Al)** is the 13th element in the periodic table and belongs to group 13.
 
• It has **three valence electrons** in its outermost shell, which is characteristic of group 13 elements.
 
• Valence electrons in Aluminum play a key role in its chemical reactivity and bonding.
 
• These three valence electrons make Aluminum a trivalent metal, forming compounds like Al₂O₃ (aluminum oxide).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table**

 
 
• The periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing atomic number and groups with similar properties.
 
• Group 13 elements include Boron (B), Aluminum (Al), Gallium (Ga), Indium (In), and Thallium (Tl).
 
• These elements typically have three electrons in their outermost shell.
 
 
 
• **Valence Electrons**
 
 
• Valence electrons are the electrons in the outermost shell of an atom.
 
• They are important in determining how an element reacts chemically with other elements.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reactivity**
 
 
• Aluminum is a reactive metal, especially at higher temperatures.
 
• It can form compounds with both metals and non-metals.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Aluminum**
 
 
• Due to its light weight, strength, and resistance to corrosion, Aluminum is used in a wide range of industries, including aerospace, automotive, and packaging.
